summary: In this excerpt from Cory Doctorow's Little Brother (Book 1, part 112), Marcus and Ange discuss the press ignoring the protesters' side of the story after hundreds were arrested. Marcus shows Ange saved blogs, videos and photostreams documenting gassing, beatings, and peaceful protest, and Ange proposes compiling everything into one linked place for reporters. Marcus, known online as M1k3y, becomes convinced the DHS has identified him, walks off in panic, and Ange chases him onto Market Street, where he contemplates throwing himself in front of a Muni trolley.
one_line: Marcus and Ange discuss the press ignoring protest accounts and plan a compiled resource, until Marcus panics that the DHS has identified him as M1k3y.
key_facts: Eight hundred people were arrested as "rioters" and no one was telling the protesters' side.
Marcus had saved blogs, videos and photostreams to his phone and showed them to Ange.
The first-hand accounts described people who had been gassed and beaten up.
The video showed dancing, peaceful political speeches, and the chant of "Take It Back."
Trudy Doo said the protesters were the only generation that could believe in fighting for their freedoms.
Ange asked why the press doesn't publish the protesters' side, and Marcus answered that reporters are whores.
Ange argued that the press could sell more papers and commercials with a controversy, since controversy is bigger than a crime.
Marcus said reporters can barely search regular blogs, let alone keep track of the Xnet.
Ange proposed writing everything up in one place with all the links, intended for the press to find, and linking it to the HOWTOs for Xnet.
Ange said Internet users can reach the Xnet provided they don't care about the DHS finding out what they've been surfing.
Ange asked, "Who wouldn't listen to M1k3y?"
Marcus believed the DHS knew who M1k3y was, and that he had been doomed since the DHS let him go from its truck.
Marcus feared the DHS would arrest him and send him away forever, to wherever Darryl had gone.
Ange nearly tackled Marcus as he reached Market Street and asked what his problem was.
Marcus felt he had a mad desire to jump in front of a Muni trolley, reasoning it was better to die than go back.
